portName: CentrePort Wellington (Aotea Quay; smaller ships at Queens Wharf)
timezone: NZST (UTC+12), NZDT (UTC+13) from late September to early April
seoTitle: Wellington cruise port guide: shuttle, cable car, Te Papa
seoDescription: Big ships berth at Aotea Quay, 1.5 km out; a shuttle runs to Wakefield St. Cable car NZ$13 return, Te Papa NZ$35 for visitors (2026). No taxis at the wharf.
quickAnswer: Most ships berth at Aotea Quay inside CentrePort, about 1.5 km north of the city centre, and passengers ride the cruise shuttle to Wakefield Street, opposite the Amora Hotel, in about 10–15 minutes. Taxis cannot pick up or drop off at the wharf, so the shuttle is your way back too. Be at the Wakefield Street stop 90 minutes before all-aboard so you are on board an hour before.
intro: Wellington is a compact, walkable capital wrapped around a harbour, with most of what a cruise visitor wants within 20 minutes' walk of the shuttle stop: Te Papa, the waterfront, the cable car up to the Botanic Garden, and the cafés and bars of Cuba Street. The catch is that the main cruise berth sits in the working port, so you depend on the shuttle in both directions. Ships usually stay about eight hours. The weather changes fast and the wind is strong, so bring a layer even on a sunny morning.

terminals.name: Aotea Quay (CentrePort)
terminals.notes: Main berth for large ships, inside the working port with no public access. The cruise zone has toilets, a gift shop, a convenience store, shelter, an information centre, free Wi-Fi and seating, with city ambassadors on hand. Passengers leave by the cruise shuttle or a tour coach; taxis cannot collect or drop off at the wharf.

terminals.name: Queens Wharf
terminals.notes: Downtown waterfront berth used by smaller ships. From here you walk straight onto the waterfront and into the city centre. Your ship will tell you which berth it uses.

walkability.detail: From Aotea Quay you take the cruise shuttle; ask your ship on the day whether any walking route is open. From the Wakefield Street shuttle stop, or from Queens Wharf, the city centre is flat and compact: Te Papa, the waterfront and Lambton Quay are all a short walk.

transportSections.detail: Ship staff direct you to the shuttle on arrival. It passes the stadium and Wellington Railway Station and stops on Wakefield Street, opposite the Amora Hotel, near the i-SITE and Te Papa. The same stop is the pick-up point back to the ship.

transportSections.cost: NZ$7 one way, NZ$13 return adult (2026)
transportSections.detail: Lower terminal at Cable Car Lane, 280 Lambton Quay. Opens 07:30 Monday to Friday and 08:30 at weekends and on public holidays. Buy tickets online or at the ticket box; Snapper cards are not accepted. Expect queues on ship days.

transportSections.cost: Fares by zone; adult tap-on with a contactless card or phone, cash still accepted on board (2026)
transportSections.detail: Since April 2026 adults can tap on and off with a debit or credit card, phone or watch. Cash is being phased out by March 2027. Useful for Zealandia (stops about 5 minutes' walk away) and the eastern suburbs.
Electric shuttles run to Zealandia from Wakefield Street and from the top of the Cable Car.
Taxis cannot enter the cruise wharf at Aotea Quay. Use them around the city, and get dropped at the Wakefield Street shuttle stop to return.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the Wakefield Street shuttle stop 90 minutes before all-aboard, so you are on board 60 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: There is no other way back to Aotea Quay: taxis and private cars cannot drop off at the wharf. If an independent tour company will not take you to the wharf, ask to be dropped at the shuttle stop with time to catch a shuttle. Ships at Queens Wharf: walk back and be on board 60 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you are late, take a taxi to the Wakefield Street shuttle stop and call the port agent number on your daily programme. City ambassadors in black and yellow can point you to the stop.

diyVsExcursion.item: City highlights: cable car, Botanic Garden, Te Papa
diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Cable car NZ$13 return plus Te Papa NZ$35 for international visitors (2026)

excursionAdvice: Wellington's centre is easy to do alone from the shuttle stop: cable car, Botanic Garden, Te Papa and the waterfront need no guide. A tour earns its place for things further out: Wētā Workshop in Miramar, Mount Victoria lookout if you do not want the climb, and seal-colony trips on the south coast. Tours that leave from the ship also bring you back to it, which removes the shuttle question. Popular independent tours sell out, so book before you arrive.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship berths at Aotea Quay at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Take the cruise shuttle to Wakefield Street, opposite the Amora Hotel.
Walk to the cable car's lower terminal at 280 Lambton Quay.
Ride up to Kelburn. See the Cable Car Museum and the view, then walk down through the Wellington Botanic Garden.
Te Papa (opens 10:00). Allow two hours for the permanent galleries.
Lunch and coffee on or around Cuba Street.
Walk the waterfront east towards Oriental Bay.
At the shuttle stop, 90 minutes before all-aboard.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Te Papa Tongarewa (Museum of New Zealand)
sights.why: National museum covering Māori culture, New Zealand history and natural history, with many interactive exhibits.
sights.cost: NZ$35 for international visitors aged 16 and over; under-16s free (2026)
sights.tip: Open daily 10:00–18:00. Book a time slot online to skip the queue; the ticket is valid for 48 hours.

sights.name: Wellington Cable Car
sights.why: Running since 1902 from Lambton Quay up to Kelburn, with a view over the city and harbour.
sights.timeNeeded: 1 hour including the museum at the top
sights.tip: Ride up and walk down through the Botanic Garden to save the return fare and the queue.

sights.name: Wellington Botanic Garden
sights.why: Hillside gardens between the top of the cable car and the city.
sights.tip: Space Place observatory and the Cable Car Museum are at the top.

sights.name: Zealandia
sights.why: Fenced ecosanctuary close to the city where native birds and reptiles live free of introduced predators.
sights.tip: Use the free electric shuttle from Wakefield Street or the top of the cable car.

sights.name: Waterfront and Oriental Bay
sights.why: Harbourside walk from Queens Wharf past Te Papa to the city's sandy beach.
sights.tip: Good in sun; very exposed when the wind is up.

sights.name: Mount Victoria lookout
sights.why: The best view over the city and harbour; the slopes were also a Lord of the Rings filming location.
sights.timeNeeded: 1.5–2 hours on foot; less by taxi or tour
sights.tip: Walk up via the trails, or take a taxi up and walk down.

sights.name: Wētā Workshop
sights.why: Tours of the film-effects company in Miramar, focused on prop design and film-making.
sights.tip: Book in advance; tours often sell out on ship days.

sights.name: Cuba Street
sights.why: The city's café, bar and independent shop street.
sights.tip: A natural lunch stop between Te Papa and the shuttle stop.

beaches.name: Oriental Bay
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk east along the waterfront from Te Papa
beaches.note: The city's beach, beside the waterfront promenade, with harbour views.

food.dish: Flat white and a cheese scone
food.where: Cafés on Cuba Street and around Lambton Quay
Craft beer bars in the city centre, especially around Cuba Street
Waterfront restaurants between Queens Wharf and Oriental Bay

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to take a taxi back to the ship at Aotea Quay.
commonMistakes.fix: Taxis cannot drop off at the wharf. Return to the Wakefield Street shuttle stop instead.
International visitors aged 16 and over pay NZ$35 (2026). Entry is free for New Zealanders and residents.
It opens at 10:00. Do the cable car and Botanic Garden first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying cash on the cable car at Lambton Quay.
commonMistakes.fix: Buy online or at the ticket box; Snapper is not accepted.

commonMistakes.mistake: Booking Wētā Workshop or a popular tour on the day.
commonMistakes.fix: Book before you arrive; there is no booking desk at CentrePort.
Wellington is windy and the weather changes quickly. Carry a warm, windproof layer.

safety: Wellington is a safe city for visitors. Normal precautions apply in busy areas and at night. The main practical risks are the wind on exposed waterfront and hilltop paths, sudden weather changes, and the need to get back to the shuttle stop on time. City ambassadors in black and yellow work on ship days and can give directions and a cruise map.
accessibility: The city centre and waterfront are flat. The cable car is a short ride but the Botanic Garden and Mount Victoria are steep. Check with your ship about wheelchair access on the cruise shuttle. At Queens Wharf the walk into town is level.
rainyDay: Te Papa can fill a wet morning on its own, and its ticket is valid for 48 hours. Add the Cable Car Museum at the top of the cable car, and cafés on Cuba Street. Skip Mount Victoria and the Botanic Garden in strong wind or heavy rain.
crowdTips: Ships carry up to about 4,900 passengers, and cable car visitor numbers double on ship days. Go to the cable car first thing, before Te Papa opens at 10:00, then do Te Papa while the queue for the cable car peaks. Book a Te Papa time slot online. Leave for the shuttle stop early: everyone heads back at the same time.

faqs.q: Is Wellington walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: From Aotea Quay, no: the berth is inside the working port and you take the cruise shuttle to Wakefield Street. From Queens Wharf you walk straight into the centre.

faqs.q: How do I get from Wellington cruise port to the city centre?
faqs.a: Take the cruise shuttle from Aotea Quay. It takes about 10–15 minutes and stops on Wakefield Street opposite the Amora Hotel, near Te Papa and the i-SITE.
No. Ships berth at Aotea Quay or, if smaller, Queens Wharf.

faqs.q: Can I get a taxi back to the ship in Wellington?
faqs.a: Not to the wharf. Taxis cannot pick up or drop off at the cruise berth; go to the shuttle stop.

faqs.q: What can I do in Wellington in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Ride the cable car up, walk down through the Botanic Garden, spend two hours at Te Papa, then lunch on Cuba Street and a waterfront walk.

faqs.q: How much is Te Papa for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: NZ$35 for international visitors aged 16 and over; under-16s are free (2026). Open 10:00–18:00 daily.
Oriental Bay is the city beach, along the waterfront east of Te Papa.
Yes. Take normal precautions and dress for wind and changeable weather.
